reasoning:
Count subsets of {1..25} with sum 100 by size m. An m-subset summing to 100 corresponds (subtract 1,2,...,m from sorted elements) to a partition of T = 100 - m(m+1)/2 into at most m parts each <= 25-m. Feasible sizes: m = 5..13 (min sum 91 for m=13, max sum 94 for m=4).

For each m I computed B(T; m, 25-m) = p_m(T) - #(partitions of T into <= m parts with largest part >= 26-m), where p_m(n) = partitions of n into parts <= m (built tables p_3..p_10 up to n=64 via p_k(n)=p_k(n-k)+p_{k-1}(n), checked against known values like p_7(40)=6430, p_8(40)=9749), and the subtracted term is a sum over the largest part L of box-restricted partitions of T-L into <= m-1 parts, with small nested corrections where T-L > L.

Results:
m=5: T=85 (complement 15 in 5x20 box) -> p_5(15) = 84
m=6: T=79 (complement 35 in 6x19) -> 2172 - 408 = 1764
m=7: T=72 (complement 54 in 7x18) -> p_7(54)=26226 minus 16328 = 9898
m=8: T=64 in 8x17 -> p_8(64)=116263 minus 92276 = 23987
m=9: T=55 in 9x16 -> p_9(55)=79403 minus 50051 = 29352
m=10: T=45 in 10x15 -> p_10(45)=33401 minus 14547 = 18854 (cross-checked by full inclusion-exclusion from p(45)=89134)
m=11: T=34 in 11x14 -> p_11(34)=7972 minus 1891 = 6081
m=12: T=22 in 12x13 -> 905 - 67 = 838
m=13: T=9 -> p(9) = 30

Total = 84+1764+9898+23987+29352+18854+6081+838+30 = 90888.
(Sanity: normal approximation with mean 162.5, sd ~37.2 gives ~89k.)
